question: In a fixed coordinate system, do the coordinates of a fixed free vector depend on where its initial point is placed?
solution: If the endpoints are \(A\) and \(B\), the vector is \(B-A\). Translating both endpoints by the same vector \(t\) gives \((B+t)-(A+t)=B-A\). Thus a fixed free vector has the same coordinates wherever it is placed. In fixed axes, its coordinates depend on both magnitude and direction. A is correct.
